headline: Explicit models recover haplotypes, linkage disequilibrium and unsampled tree regions
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: Three new preprints apply explicit formulations to pangenome graphs, viral short reads and partially sampled pathogen phylogenies.
synthesis: The common thread is replacing an implicit or simplifying step with an explicit formulation of the unobserved quantity. DiGi casts diploid genotyping on a pangenome haplotype trellis graph as an exact integer program, inferring two haplotype paths jointly from reads. LDEN estimates whole-genome linkage disequilibrium from short-read viral sequencing data by alternating projections onto positive semidefinite matrices, so the target quantity is fitted under explicit constraints rather than read off directly. The pathogen phylogenetics item localizes unsampled regions from the observed tree alone using machine learning and beam search. What is new is the target: haplotype configurations, genome-wide linkage structure and unsampled portions of a phylogeny are each treated as latent objects to be inferred. The third item relies on a learned search rather than an exact or convex formulation, so its shared logic with the first two is weaker.
